key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% versus bare SA516 boiler steel during cyclic testing at 900°C.
engineering_relevance: This coating offers a promising route to improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of SA516 boiler components.
method: Apply Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Expose coated and bare steel to 50 air-oxidation cycles at 900°C.
Characterize phases and microstructure using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The HVOF Ni–20Cr+40TiC coating showed the largest reported weight-gain reduction, while bare steel developed severe oxide spalling, cracking, and nonprotective Fe₂O₃.
watch_item: Results are limited to laboratory air oxidation; long-term performance in corrosive boiler atmospheres remains unverified.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
